title: #006. 0-1 Project Selection (Binary Variables)
subtitle: Model all-or-nothing R&D investment choices using 0-1 binary decision variables.
markdown:
# #006. 0-1 Project Selection (Binary Variables)

<!-- section:scenario -->
A product team has $n$ candidate projects $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Each project is strictly **all-or-nothing** (`selected[i]` $\in \{0, 1\}$): funding it consumes `costs[i]` of the limited `budget` and delivers strategic value `values[i]`.

Choose which projects to approve to **maximize total value** without exceeding `budget`.

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P006Input`)**: `budget: number`, `costs: number[]`, `values: number[]`
- **Output (`P006Output`)**: `{ selected: number[], totalValue: number }` (every `selected[i]` must be `0` or `1`)

<!-- section:example -->
With `budget = 15`, `costs = [4, 5, 7, 3, 6]`, `values = [10, 12, 16, 8, 13]`:

- Picking strictly by highest value/cost ratio (`#3 -> #0 -> #1`) spends `3 + 4 + 5 = 12` for value `30`, leaving `3` budget unused because no remaining project costs `<= 3`.
- Picking **`selected = [0, 1, 1, 1, 0]`** (projects 1, 2, 3) spends all `5 + 7 + 3 = 15` budget for maximum value **`36`**!

<!-- section:hint1 -->
The binary array `selected` (`m.binary(...)` in WaSHI / `h.addBinary(...)` in Python) is already declared. Add the single linear inequality `dot(input.costs, selected) <= input.budget` and maximize `dot(input.values, selected)`.

<!-- section:hint2 -->
When reading solved binary variables into `{ selected, totalValue }`, apply `Math.round(v.value!)` (`round(h.val(v))` in Python) so floating-point values like `0.999999999` or `-0` normalize cleanly to `0` or `1`.

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\max \quad & \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} v_i x_i \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} c_i x_i \le B \\
& x_i \in \{0, 1\} && \forall i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}
\end{aligned}
$$

judge.m0: Output must be an object { selected, totalValue }.
judge.m3: Reported totalValue ({p0}) does not match sum of selected project values ({p1}).
judge.m4: Valid portfolio within budget, but totalValue ({p0}) is below optimal ({p1}).
